protocol.scope: consolidated digest of pre-existing 2026-10-13/14 scouts plus the Q16 focus additions

claims.reference: Liu, Y. & Tsyvinski, A. (2018/2021), 'Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency', Review of Financial Studies 34(6), 2689-2727
claims.claim: Crypto excess returns are explained by exposure to market, momentum, and (weakly) value factors; attention proxies forecast returns.
claims.rationale: Period ends 2018; pre-SUI/AAVE/NEAR/BNB. Crypto 1.0 sample is not the current market structure. The attention proxy is a non-tradable feature.

claims.reference: Han, C., Kang, B. & Ryu, J. (2024 working paper, accepted RAPS), 'Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market: A Comprehensive Analysis under Realistic Assumptions', SSRN 4675565
claims.claim: Best TSMOM config 28d lookback / 5d holding; Sharpe 1.51 vs 0.84 market portfolio; 15 bp/trade assumed cost. Weak cross-sectional momentum. Liquid coins show momentum; illiquid show daily reversal.
claims.rationale: Long sample covers the entire R2 pre-cutoff window. Config 28/5 is publishable but pre-2022. The 15 bp/trade is a literature floor; the desk cost is 8-10 bp maker / 10-12 bp taker from Q2 cost grid (no impact). After realistic costs the TSMOM Sharpe often collapses. Already explored on BTC (ledger H-20261013-001 rejected on drawdown floor). The 28/5 alt panel is still untested in our ledger.

claims.reference: Shen, D., Urquhart, A. & Wang, P. (2022), 'Bitcoin intraday time-series momentum', Financial Review 57, 319-344
claims.claim: Intraday TSMOM on 30-min bars (long/flat or long/short) earns significant Sharpe in early hours, attributed to liquidity provision rather than informed trading.
claims.rationale: Sample ends 2019; intraday crypto microstructure has changed substantially (perps dominance, ETF impact, HFT arbitrage on the 1-minute bar). Conflicting with the 2026-10-14 axe-1 finding that 1-minute BTC autocorr turned positive in 2022-2023. The signal as published is pre-mature-arbitrage.

claims.reference: Baur, D. G., Cahill, D., Godfrey, K. & Liu, Z. (2019), 'Bitcoin time-of-day, day-of-week and month-of-year effects in returns and trading volume', Finance Research Letters 31, 78-92
claims.claim: BTC has a U-shape intraday return pattern (low in Asian hours, high in EU/US hours); day-of-week and month-of-year effects exist but are not robust to controls.
claims.rationale: Directly tested in the desk's 2026-10-14 axe-1 / N0; no actionable intraday session pattern on BTC or alts. Pre-2018 sample is not current.

claims.reference: Easley, D., O'Hara, M., Yang, S. & Zhang, Z. (2024-2026 working paper), 'Microstructure and Market Dynamics in Crypto Markets', SSRN 4814346
claims.claim: Roll measure, Roll impact, Kyle's lambda, Amihud, VPIN computed on 1-min klines have non-trivial predictive power (AUC 0.55-0.58) for sign of RV change and autocorr. No P&L, no Sharpe reported.
claims.rationale: Partially replicable: Roll, Amihud, skewness, kurtosis computable on R2 klines; Kyle's lambda and VPIN require tick data. Most predictive features are notifiable as proxies, not direct microstructure. Crucially, the paper reports AUC but no P&L. Coherent with our Q11/Q12/Q13 nulls on the alt panel.

claims.reference: He, S., Manela, A., Ross, O. & von Wachter, V. (2024), 'Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures', arXiv:2212.06888
claims.claim: Funding rates in perpetual futures are a *push* mechanism designed to compress perp-spot basis; they are not a free-lunch directional signal. The carry trade requires basis convergence, which is uncertain.
claims.rationale: Directly supports the Q8 finding (persistent positive funding, no net strategy) and the funding_carry_dn ledger rejection. Not a tradable signal, but the strongest argument *against* treating funding as a directional alpha.

claims.reference: Kim, C. & Hansen, P. R. (2026), 'The Quarter-Hour Effect: Periodic Algorithmic Trading and Return Predictability in Cryptocurrency Futures', arXiv:2607.09426v2
claims.claim: Predictable patterns at the 00, 08, 16 UTC fixings in BTC perp due to scheduled algo activity; small but present.
claims.on_existing_panel: partial (R2 8h funding fixings present, intraday perp prices not in R2)
claims.rationale: Sample extends post-cutoff. R2 has funding fixings at 00/08/16 UTC, so the 8h bucket is observable; sub-8h fixing seasonality is not. A 8h-fixings-only test is a partial replication and cannot discriminate the published effect.

claims.reference: Zaremba, A. et al. (2021), 'Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets', SSRN
claims.claim: Cross-sectional short-term reversal and momentum in crypto; results sensitive to liquidity bucket.
claims.rationale: Cross-section reversal on the 8-asset alt panel is the natural Q14-style test. Already explored in Q13/Q14; the panel FE finds no significant within-entity cross-sectional alpha. No new candidate.

claims.reference: van Kyle (web replication note, 2026), 'Order-Flow Imbalance and the Decay of Price Impact'
claims.claim: Negative 3-day BTCUSDT replication: a one-minute taker-flow continuation rule loses; Kyle-style impact is contemporaneous and transient.
claims.rationale: Web replication, not peer-reviewed. Negative result on 3 days is illustrative, not a falsification framework. Consistent with Q6 descriptive null on BTC aggTrades.

claims.reference: Man Group / AHL public factor research (2024-2026) on crypto momentum and carry, public letters and Factor Research notes
claims.claim: Man AHL public factor notes (2024-2026) describe carry and momentum as the most robust factors across asset classes, with crypto carry 'compress[ing]' post-2022. No explicit Sharpe figure published.
claims.rationale: Marketing-grade evidence only. Consistent with the funding compression that Q8 documents. Not a tradable signal.

top3_rationale: No surveyed paper meets the prereg bar (real cost-aware Sharpe, 2018-2024 period, replicable on R2 klines pre-cutoff). The closest candidate is Han et al. C02 (TSMOM 28/5) but the desk's own BTC TSMOM 60d test was rejected on the drawdown floor (H-20261013-001) and the alt panel 28/5 grid is not pre-registered. The second-closest is Zaremba C08 (cross-section reversal) but the Q13/Q14 panel tests found no significant within-entity cross-sectional alpha. The third-closest is He et al. C06 (perpetual fundamentals) but the result is *anti*-alpha, not alpha. Three new Q16a/b/c sub-items are NOT added; Q16 closes with an empty replication queue and a clear note that the klines-1m pre-cutoff panel has been exhausted of literature-cited candidates.
